title: Trilateral Commission North America governance chronology, 2016–2025
summary: Dated Form 990 governance chronology separating U.S. North American legal-entity officers/trustees from current Commission regional leadership and Executive Committee roles.

sources.title: Trilateral Commission North America - Nonprofit Explorer

evidence.observation: FY2016 and FY2017 Form 990 extracted tables list Joseph S. Nye Jr. as Chairman, Michael J. O'Neil as President & Treasurer, and Mary M. Valder as Secretary.
FY2018-FY2020 extracted tables list Meghan O'Sullivan as Chair; FY2020 marks O'Neil outgoing and first lists Richard Fontaine as Executive Director.
Fontaine is listed as Executive Director with compensation of $40,000 in FY2020, $73,333 in FY2021, $95,000 in FY2022, $110,000 in FY2023 and FY2024, and $125,000 in FY2025.

North American trustee names rotate across filing years: Karen Elliott House, Marc/B. Marc Allen, Catherine Bertini, Carla A. Hills, Esther Brimmer, and Joseph S. Nye Jr.; FY2025 marks Nye as trustee until 5/25.

The current Commission page separately describes regional chairs/deputies/executive directors and a 74-member Executive Committee. These website governance categories are not interchangeable with officers/trustees of the U.S. tax-exempt entity.

gaps: The extracted ProPublica tables hide additional people behind 'View more people'; raw XML should be used for complete yearly officer/trustee enumeration.
Pre-FY2016 governance remains to be reconstructed.
Canonical identity resolution is still needed before normalized relation creation.
caveats: Form 990 roles belong to the U.S. North American legal entity and must not automatically be projected onto the global Commission.
Compensation is a filing-year observation, not a timeless salary.
Current website Executive Committee status and tax-return trustee status are distinct predicates.

workflow.next_action: Extract full raw Form 990 XML officer/trustee tables and create time-bounded governance observations through repository-scripted normalized writes.

notes: Nye is filing-listed chairman in FY2016-17; O'Sullivan is chair by FY2018 and remains listed through FY2020.
FY2020 records the operational handoff from outgoing O'Neil to Richard Fontaine as Executive Director.
Trustee membership rotates substantially across filings and must be time-bounded.
Tax-return trustees/officers must remain semantically separate from the Commission's website Executive Committee.

classification_rules: Tie Form 990 officer/trustee roles to the North American legal entity and filing year.
Preserve exact filing role labels and transition qualifiers.
Do not equate tax-return trustee with Commission Executive Committee unless explicitly supported.
Resolve identities before normalized graph writes.
data.method: Compared IRS-derived Form 990 officer/trustee and compensation tables from FY2016 through FY2025 and cross-checked current Commission leadership semantics.
data.research_question: How did the U.S. North American legal entity's officers and trustees change from FY2016 through FY2025, and how should those roles differ from current Commission leadership/Executive Committee roles?

findings.finding: Joseph S. Nye Jr. is filing-listed Chairman in FY2016 and FY2017; Meghan O'Sullivan is filing-listed Chair by FY2018 through FY2020.
FY2020 marks Michael J. O'Neil as outgoing President & Treasurer and introduces Richard Fontaine as Executive Director.
Fontaine remains filing-listed Executive Director through FY2025 with increasing annual compensation observations.
North American trustees rotate across filing years, requiring time-bounded trustee relations.
Tax-return trustees/officers and the Commission's current Executive Committee/leadership categories are overlapping but distinct governance surfaces.
